svg.title: B1.04 · Rearrange Products Table
svg.desc: One row per available product and store pair. Both products have a store1 price, 95 and 70. The quoted store name becomes data in the output. Only product 0 has a store2 price (100). Product 1's missing price removes that pair. Both products supply a row: 105 for product 0 and 80 for product 1. 2 + 1 + 2 = 5 available pairs. The store order is specified. Products tied within a store may appear in either order. Each branch · FROM Products. All three store prices are already on each product row. Read one store column per branch so a product can contribute a separate row to every store that has a price. UNION ALL · stack the three stores. The result needs one row per available product and store. Appending the independent branches preserves all five pairs without a join. The final sort sets the display order.
svg.text: One row per available product and store pair.
Two products have three store columns each. Why do we get five price rows?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.

g.text: All three store prices are already on each product row. Read one store column per branch so a product can contribute a
separate row to every store that has a price.

svg.text: Both products have a store1 price, 95 and 70. The quoted store name becomes data in the output.
SELECT product_id, 'store1' AS store, store1 AS price … WHERE store1 IS NOT NULL
Which product is available at store2?
Only product 0 has a store2 price (100). Product 1's missing price removes that pair.
SELECT product_id, 'store2' AS store, store2 AS price … WHERE store2 IS NOT NULL
Which products are available at store3?
Both products supply a row: 105 for product 0 and 80 for product 1.
SELECT product_id, 'store3' AS store, store3 AS price … WHERE store3 IS NOT NULL
Why stack the three sets of rows?

g.aria-label: UNION ALL · stack the three stores
g.text: UNION ALL · stack the three stores
The result needs one row per available product and store. Appending the independent branches preserves all five pairs
without a join. The final sort sets the display order.

svg.text: 2 + 1 + 2 = 5 available pairs. The store order is specified. Products tied within a store may appear in either order.
UNION ALL / ORDER BY store ASC
